label: final copy step of length-3 sequences (outputting the 3rd token)
explanation: Active only during the copy phase. It never fires on original or delimiter steps. About two-thirds of the activation mass, including nearly all of the top examples, is at the last step of L=3 sequences (t=5, input orig(1), output orig(2)). There it fires on about 59% of sequences, and token identity sets both whether it fires and how strongly: first tokens u/w/e/z/g/o/b give about 84% precision, while f/y/t/n/i/h/3 rarely fire. Weaker secondary firing: the penultimate step of L=4 (t=6, recall_idx 2, about 11% of mass) and the last two steps of L=9 (t=16-17, about 16% of mass, but only about 3% of those steps fire), plus scattered low-magnitude late-copy steps at L=6-8. Overall it is a sparse, token-gated end-of-copy signal; adding the L=4 and L=9 clauses raises mass recall to 0.90 but drops precision to 0.08.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=17: i, m, l, j; t=16: j, i, m, g; t=12: l, m, r, i) and the previous input (most: b, e, z, u, g, w; least: 1, y, r, x); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=3, L=4 & t=6.
